title: Metaphor, Question, Repetition: Making a Point

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *El tiempo es un río* from B2 Unit 36. Three devices are easy to spot: a metaphor says one thing *is* another, without *como* (*El tiempo es un río*); a rhetorical question is asked to make a point, not to get an answer (*¿Quién puede negar que los precios suben?*); repetition stresses an idea (*Trabajo, trabajo y más trabajo*). Writing about identity uses them all.

items.spanish: América Latina es un mosaico de lenguas y culturas.
items.english: Latin America is a mosaic of languages and cultures. (metaphor)

items.spanish: ¿Quién puede negar que la región es diversa?
items.english: Who can deny that the region is diverse? (rhetorical question)

items.spanish: Lenguas, lenguas y más lenguas: así es el continente.
items.english: Languages, languages and more languages: that is the continent. (repetition)

items.spanish: La región no es como un mosaico: es un mosaico.
items.english: The region is not like a mosaic: it is a mosaic. (the first half is a comparison, the second a metaphor)

sections.content: Use one device at a time. A sentence with *como* is a comparison, not a metaphor. A rhetorical question works best when the answer is obvious. If a plain sentence says it better, keep the plain sentence.
